hero.title: Urban Centers of Gupta Age
hero.description: A study of the paradox of urban decline and the socio-economic structure of cities in the Gupta period.

timeline.title: Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Tracing the urban trajectory from the peak of classical urbanism to the onset of the early medieval transition.

cards.details: Prosperity under Samudragupta and Chandragupta II; bustling trade and high urban activity.
Signs of decay begin; Fa-Hien observes flourishing cities like Pataliputra.
Huna invasions and economic decentralization leading to 'Urban Decay'.

items.title: P.A.T.H
items.decryption: Pataliputra as capital; Administrative centralization; Trade (Internal/External); Huna pressure leading to decline.

traps.title: UPSC Exam Traps
items: Assuming 'Golden Age' implies continuous urban growth; R.S. Sharma argues for 'Urban Decay' in the late Gupta period.
Confusing Pataliputra's decline with the total abandonment of cities; some cities shifted towards temple-centric centers.

deepDive.description: Master the key concepts and dimensions of this topic.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Gangetic Heartland (Pataliputra)
  • Coastal ports (Tamralipti)
  • Trade nodes (Ujjain, Mathura)

Personalities

  • Fa-Hien (Chinese pilgrim)
  • Kalidasa (City life descriptions)
  • Gupta Bureaucrats (City administration)

Socio-Economic Mindmap

  • Urban Decline Hypothesis (R.S. Sharma)
    • Economic Factors: Decline of long-distance trade.
    • Social Factors: Rise of landed intermediaries (Samantas).
    • Political Factors: Decentralization of power.
  • City Administration
    • Purapala: City governor.
    • Nagarsreshti: Head of guilds/merchants.
    • Sarthavaha: Caravan leader.
